title: Old-time parade clothes, umbrellas and the rough second line
summary: Old parade dress was black suits; umbrellas and baskets cost a lot, and rough second liners trouble the parade.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: In olden times, did they spend much money on their clothes when they had the thick hair?

Well, the... Marais, I mean? No, they mostly, in olden times, when they turned out, they had black suits. They didn't turn out like these fellas turn out the day, but they all decorate umbrellas. You know how it cost them 15, 12 dollars to decorate one of them umbrellas? I'm telling you. Fans, they decorate their fans in the umbrellas. They have a fan umbrella and a basket. That's right. I want to see how they carry it all. Well, it's sad. They'll be having it. They don't need all that. I wouldn't want an umbrella in a basket, me, myself. But they'll have it. You'll see them if you live long enough. You'll see them in an umbrella and a basket. I was talking about how much it's going to cost them to every is umbrella made. But I never didn't have a basket. I only had a fan. Because I've been an officer for years, too. I was just riding an automobile. Yeah, I'd ride an automobile and get tired and we'd just cut out. If we got to stop, say, 10 blocks away, well, we'll just go there and get out the automobile and get a couple of beers and wait until they get there. And every one fault I find I would raise a second line. We just get them guys off the street. They're all right, but I don't know, you just can't get them out the street. The police can't do nothing with them.
It cost you a thousand dollars to hire enough policemen to take them away.

That's right. That's really a fact. You never have many police, you've got to have your help in the parade. When they get in that procession, and as you go along, you're picking them up. About a 20, 150 cent. They got a gang down there that's the umbrella game. They comes out with their own umbrellas. Well, I've seen that crowd and they can really be kind of rough. They is rough. They too rough. And that's the street not on food with them because they too rough. They don't worry me because I don't parade. And I hasn't been parading. They asked me, Mice asked me, was I coming out? I said, no indeed. Mice thinks this is the fifth year I am parading. It's the sixth year. I said, I don't know what to do. What are you going to do? They put them in jail and all that. That's what's to use. It's just a rough gang. And I was in hope they would never parade no more myself. I said, I have to go up there. I'll be up there and see them all. And to see if they get everything arranged right and that. I'll go back. We had a dance at night, you know. And I'll go back and be at the dance. Mice is chairman of the dance. He's going to parade. Mice is chairman of the dance. He's assistant chairman of the parade. I don't see how he can make it all that. Well, I'll tell you how they wake that out. He's an officer. He rides mostly at the time. And around about 4 o'clock, 4.30, when he'll cut out, go home and think. He wants to come back until about 9, 10 o'clock. He's got an assistant who was really everything arranged before the parade. And his assistant won't parade. You see, he'll be right on the job. We have a standard committee, yearly committee. And they take care of everything. So we just appointed chairman for the Sunshine of the Enterprise. And those fellas take over. Is that the name, Bella? Yeah, they take over. Ice up, beer up, then put behind the ball. They're very dutiful. They like to help their club out. Yeah.
